items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: I didn't get the opportunity to meet too many of the younger drummers. Like Kenny Clarke, he was a very good drummer.

ctx.x: Okay, then that was that same session. Now, up until this time, of course, there's a new type of music in Jazz that is on the scene, with some younger musicians, and they had their special way of playing the drums, and there were drummers like Kenny Clarke and Max Roach, among others. Did you get an opportunity to hear these younger drummers? And what was your reaction to them? What did you think of them?

Well, I didn't get the opportunity to meet too many of the younger drummers. Like Kenny Clarke, he was a very good drummer. And there was a drummer who was living over... I think he passed away. He was in Paris there for a while. But he wasn't necessarily a younger drummer; but he had a lot of experience. It will come to me after a while, what that boy's name is over in Paris, France. He had just come out of the Army.

Well, a lot of the... Max Roach and Kenny Clarke are two of the drummers who, being involved with the music of, say, Charlie Parker and Dizzy Come, also paid a great deal of respect to Big Sid Catlett.
